definition: Environmental design is the planning or shaping of surroundings to support health and recovery. In this context, it refers to using features such as natural-looking virtual settings to improve therapeutic experiences and public health outcomes.

reasons: The definition gives a broad general meaning for “environmental design” (“planning or shaping of surroundings to support health and recovery”) that is not stated in the packet as a definition of the term.

The packet only supports a narrower research context involving virtual reality, therapeutic landscapes, and public health; it does not establish that environmental design itself means using natural-looking virtual settings.
“Public health outcomes” and “therapeutic experiences” are plausible paraphrases of the study’s aims, but the wording overgeneralizes beyond what the source directly supports.

The definition’s first sentence (“Environmental design is the planning or shaping of surroundings…”) is not supported by the packet, which discusses VR as a tool within “therapeutic landscapes” and references “environmental design in the field of public health” without defining environmental design as planning/shaping surroundings.

The packet supports the idea of using virtual natural environments to aid “health recovery” in therapeutic/public-health contexts, but it does not explicitly support the broader general phrasing about environmental design generally being the planning/shaping of surroundings.
Because the core definitional framing is not evidenced in the packet, the definition cannot be accepted as a defensible, sourced definition.
